required_use_contract.instruction_text:
MANDATORY REPOSITORY-ANALYSIS PROTOCOL for this session:
1. Before you make ANY code change, call the mcp__provenlattice__query tool.
2. Request task-context facts relevant to this task: command "task-context" with the --json flag and the anchor symbol(s) you consider relevant.
3. If the tool reports that no analysis is built yet, run the tool's index command for this repository, then repeat the task-context request with --json.
4. Read the returned result carefully before continuing.
5. After the protocol steps above, complete the bugfix described below as best you can.

research_question: When repository-analysis is actually consumed by the Agent, do ProvenLattice facts improve real coding-task outcomes?
symmetry_invariants: MCP registration A==B (init event server entry + tool enumeration)
tool schema A==B (frozen C8-A tool entry bytes served by both arms)
runtime/runner code identical except treatment response source (adapter digest identical; only arm env differs)
control/treatment binding auditable via the sealed assignment artifact
no case-specific branch anywhere in adapter/runner/instruction (scan-enforced)
one invocation per planned cell; no silent retry
normalization provenance retained per cell (v2 parse states)
treatment assignment hidden from reviewers (packets blinded per frozen C6 machinery)
threats_to_validity: response size/token asymmetry is inherent to the treatment (measured, not padded)
deterministic control may signal 'tool unavailable' — agents may diverge in downstream strategy; the notice is honest and the divergence is measured
required-use changes ecological validity vs C6-C8 optional use (separate questions by design)
upstream-patch memorization may saturate task success on frozen cases (ceiling risk)
A-arm task-context interception replaces a would-fail CLI call by design; error-path behavior of a real missing command is not experienced
